Profile Likelihood Intervals

Source: R/profile_class.R
confint.StatmodProfile.Rd

Inverts the profile of each label. Writing \(\hat\ell\) for the maximum of the criterion and \(\ell_p(\theta)\) for the profile at the value \(\theta\), the interval is the set of values at which the likelihood ratio statistic \(2\{\hat\ell - \ell_p(\theta)\}\) does not exceed the quantile of a chi-squared distribution.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'StatmodProfile'
confint(
  object,
  parm = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  type = c("marginal", "simultaneous"),
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A StatmodProfile object.

parm

The labels, a subset of object@profiled_labels; by default all of them.

level

The coverage.

type

"marginal" or "simultaneous".

...

Unused.

Value

A data frame with one row for each label, named by it, and the columns estimate, lower and upper, on the scale of the profile.

Details

Between two points of the profile the limit is found by a cubic spline through the square root of the statistic, taken with the sign of \(\theta - \hat\theta\), which is close to linear in \(\theta\) where the profile is close to quadratic. A limit outside the values of the profile is NA, and the function warns.

With type = "marginal" the quantile has one degree of freedom, and each interval covers its label with probability level. With type = "simultaneous" it has \(k\) degrees of freedom, \(k\) being the number of labels of the profile. Each interval is then the projection on its label of the joint region in which the statistic of the \(k\) labels does not exceed \(\chi^2_k(\mathrm{level})\), because the profile of one label is the maximum of the criterion over the other labels, and the \(k\) intervals cover the labels jointly with probability at least level.

The profile of the position of a sharp modelterms7::jump() or modelterms7::jseg() is constant between two consecutive values of the covariate. Its interval runs from the value of the covariate below the first interval of values in which the statistic does not exceed the quantile to the value above the last one.

The one-dimensional profile of a label is exact when the labels are profiled one at a time (joint = FALSE in statmod_profile()). In a joint profile it is the maximum over the grid of the other labels, so its accuracy is limited by the spacing of that grid.

The function signals an error when the profile does not give a likelihood ratio statistic (the property is_likelihood_ratio): for the hyperparameter of a kinked penalty that a path chooses, and for a coefficient without a penalty held under reml(), where ml() gives the likelihood ratio.

See also

statmod_profile(), confint.StatmodFit().

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(60))
dd$y <- 1 + 2 * dd$x + rnorm(60, sd = 0.4)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
prof <- statmod_profile(fit, which = "mu:x",
                        values = profile_range(width = 3, n = 13))
confint(prof)
#>      estimate    lower    upper
#> mu:x 1.956143 1.622843 2.289442
